You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 3dccfecdb867fe35b305a4e493ef5652b7d9d4cb Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Soren Brinkmann <soren.brinkmann@xilinx.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jan 2015 11:05:27 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] clk: zynq: Force CPU_2X clock to be ungated

The CPU_2X clock does not have a classical in-kernel user, but is,
amongst other things, required for OCM and debug access. Make sure this
clock is not mistakenly disabled during boot up by enabling it in the
platform's clock driver.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # 3.11+
Fixes: 0ee52b157b8e 'clk: zynq: Add clock controller driver'
Signed-off-by: Soren Brinkmann <soren.brinkmann@xilinx.com>
Signed-off-by: Michael Turquette <mturquette@linaro.org>
---
 drivers/clk/zynq/clkc.c | 1 +
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)

diff --git a/drivers/clk/zynq/clkc.c b/drivers/clk/zynq/clkc.c
index 9037bebd69f7..f870aad57711 100644
--- a/drivers/clk/zynq/clkc.c
+++ b/drivers/clk/zynq/clkc.c
@@ -303,6 +303,7 @@ static void __init zynq_clk_setup(struct device_node *np)
 	clks[cpu_2x] = clk_register_gate(NULL, clk_output_name[cpu_2x],
 			"cpu_2x_div", CLK_IGNORE_UNUSED, SLCR_ARM_CLK_CTRL,
 			26, 0, &armclk_lock);
+	clk_prepare_enable(clks[cpu_2x]);
 
 	clk = clk_register_fixed_factor(NULL, "cpu_1x_div", "cpu_div", 0, 1,
 			4 + 2 * tmp);
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The CPU_2X clock was mistakenly being disabled during boot up due to the lack of a classical in-kernel user. This clock is crucial for OCM (On-Chip Memory) and debug access, and its absence would result in failure to access these functionalities, necessitating the addition of the `clk_prepare_enable` call to ensure it remains enabled during the initialization process.

You are a programming expert.
    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    
    Provide a response strictly in the following format:
    Code statements:
    <text1>
    <text2>
    <text3>
    <text4>
    ...
    <textN>

Root cause:
The CPU_2X clock was mistakenly being disabled during boot up due to the lack of a classical in-kernel user. This clock is crucial for OCM (On-Chip Memory) and debug access, and its absence would result in failure to access these functionalities, necessitating the addition of the `clk_prepare_enable` call to ensure it remains enabled during the initialization process.
